ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Figure (1), given point $O$ is the intersection point of lines $AB$ and $CD$, $\angle BOD=32^\circ$, $OE$ bisects $\angle AOD$, $\angle EOF=90^\circ$, find the degree measure of $\angle COF$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: $\because$ $\angle BOD=32^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AOD=180^\circ-\angle BOD=180^\circ-32^\circ=148^\circ$.\\
$\because$ $OE$ bisects $\angle AOD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DOE=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOD=74^\circ$.\\
$\because$ $\angle EOF=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle COF=180^\circ-\angle DOE-\angle EOF=180^\circ-74^\circ-90^\circ=\boxed{16^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure (1), given point $O$ is the intersection point of lines $AB$ and $CD$, $\angle BOD=32^\circ$, $OE$ bisects $\angle AOD$, $\angle EOF=90^\circ$, find the degree measure of $\angle COF$.
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Solution: $\because$ $\angle BOD=32^\circ$,\\ $\therefore$ $\angle AOD=180^\circ-\angle BOD=180^\circ-32^\circ=148^\circ$.\\ $\because$ $OE$ bisects $\angle AOD$,\\ $\therefore$ $\angle DOE=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOD=74^\circ$.\\ $\because$ $\angle EOF=90^\circ$,\\ $\therefore$ $\angle COF=180^\circ-\angle DOE-\angle EOF=180^\circ-74^\circ-90^\circ=\boxed{16^\circ}$
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, point O is the intersection point of two straight lines AB and CD; AB is a horizontal straight line passing through O, with A on the left and B on the right. CD is an oblique straight line passing through O, with C at the lower left and D at the upper right, therefore OC and OD are opposite rays. Ray OE extends from O toward the upper left, ray OF extends from O toward the lower left, and in the figure F is located within this semicircular range from OC to OD. The problem gives ∠BOD=32°, OE bisects ∠AOD, and ∠EOF=90°. Then reason: Because AB is a straight line, OA and OB are opposite rays, so ∠AOD and ∠BOD form a linear pair. Given ∠BOD=32°, therefore ∠AOD=180°−32°=148°. Also because OE bisects ∠AOD, ∠DOE=∠AOD/2=148°/2=74°. Since OC and OD are opposite rays, ∠COD=180°; in the semicircle from OC to OD, ∠COF, ∠FOE, and ∠EOD add up to 180°. Given ∠EOF=90°, ∠DOE=74°, so ∠COF=180°−90°−74°=16°.
